chunks: Among what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who stands in salat and does not know whether he has prayed anything or not. He said: “He starts over.”
And whoever forgets two rakʿahs from Ṣalāt al-Layl, then remembers them after having performed the witr, he repeats them and repeats the witr. He narrated that.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْوَتْرَ: the witr, the closing odd-numbered prayer of the night prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs, i.e. two units of prayer
key_terms.سَهَا: forgot or became heedless during the prayer
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: he starts afresh or begins the prayer again

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he has prayed anything, or remembers missed rakʿahs of Ṣalāt al-Layl after witr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning doubt and forgetfulness in salat. It states that one who does not know whether he has performed any part of the prayer must begin anew, and that if two rakʿahs of Ṣalāt al-Layl were omitted and only remembered after witr, those two rakʿahs and the witr are to be repeated.
